title: Smoking Sections
excerpt: I think the smoking sections at airports should be more thoughtful to the traveler.
body:
I think the smoking sections at airports should be more thoughtful to the traveler. Considering the desire associated with travel, the pressure associated with business, and the general risk involved with flying, smoking a cigarette before and after a flight should be a signature experience.

There are a few smoking sections I’ve found civilized.

In Seoul, the Incheon International Airport has transparent rectangular pods directly outside of the terminals with ashtrays and automatic doors. This is good. You arrive so disoriented from America that the pods feel like some sort of smoked drenched waiting room for you to collect yourself before heading deeper into the unknown.

Two other smoking sections that come to mind are at Bob Hope Airport (soon to be Hollywood Airport) in Burbank and Amerigo Vespucci Airport, in Florence, Italy. In Burbank, the smoking section is an all but forgotten alleyway away from the general public. It feels private, and most importantly, provides shade from the Los Angeles sun. One bench, two ashtrays, and a few plants hanging on for dear life. In Italy at the Vespucci Airport, you may smoke wherever you wish, with trash can sized ashtrays at your disposal.

While writing this seated in Jetblue Terminal 5 at LAX—whose smoking section is deplorable, resembling more of a bus stop with no bench—I realized that there is much to see and many more airports to feel out of control in. You must go through the discomfort caused in public spaces to recognize the type of person you want to be and who you want to surround yourself with. Once inside the Airport, I advise you to keep your luggage close, and consider time is best spent people watching.

Of course airports are filled with instances of mundanity and delays, and it is in these moments it would be nice to think fondly of the cigarette I just had, and my future cigarette I will inhale upon landing. I’m not enough of an addict to desire to smoke on airplanes, but a carefully considered smoking section should be a priority in America.

While on the subject, I’d like to note the few circumstances where smoking does not count.

- Pre-and-post flight
- Europe
- As an appetizer before your second martini
- After finishing the last page of a book
- on Christmas post-dinner, pre-dessert with my grandmother (that one is personal to me)
- Inside if a restaurant, bar, or club allows

Positively harmful?

Absolutely. But when the time is right, smoking a cigarette is a wonderful way to keep present. I’m not in any way insinuating that it’s as good for you as yoga, but we all know life has always been about breathing in… and out.
